findings.claim: The loop-8 ADMIN-token prerequisite probe names Task 2's hasRole rule whenever an ADMIN token is refused on /admin/**, but the same refusal happens when Task 2 is correct and Task 3's token lacks the roles claim, so the step 6 test gives a specific, false diagnosis and no row runs. Critic run at f437bce1a385be8ff0ec5a70d88a607cfd6cf3a1, JDK 25.0.5, Maven 3.9.16 offline, on the private solution with only Task 3's claim name changed from roles to role (a one-character slip against the TODO): task2ProtectsEndpointsByPathAndRole passes (it uses user().roles(), not a token); task3 fails with a NullPointerException message about getClaimAsStringList returning null; task4 fails 'expected:<200> but was:<403>'; and task7ShowsTheAttackEachPracticeStops reports only 'finish Task 2 first: an ADMIN token is refused on /admin/** (the rule should be hasRole("ADMIN"), which matches the ROLE_ADMIN authority the converter gives)'. The chain already uses hasRole("ADMIN"), and task2 passes, so the message sends the learner to a correct line. The shipped converter reads authorities from the roles claim with the ROLE_ prefix (SecurityConfig jwtAuthenticationConverter), so a token without that claim carries no ROLE_ADMIN and hasRole refuses it. earlierTasks() checks Task 3 only by issue() returning non-null. Low: it needs a deviation from the Task 3 TODO, and task3 fails in the same run.

findings.recommendation: Before the ADMIN-token probe, decode the issued ADMIN token with the context's JwtDecoder and check that its roles claim contains ADMIN; if not, return 'finish Task 3 first: the token has no roles claim with the given roles (see the TokenService TODO)'. findings.claim: The loop-8 switch of POST /auth/register from hand-written checks to @Valid with @NotBlank makes the running app answer a blank or missing field with 401 and a Bearer challenge instead of 400, so the shipped comment 'Bean Validation answers a blank field with 400 before the handler runs' (line 28) and lab-run.json's 'refuses a blank or missing password with 400' are true only under MockMvc. Critic probe at f437bce1a385be8ff0ec5a70d88a607cfd6cf3a1: a scratch @SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT) test on the solved work, sending real HTTP with java.net.http.HttpClient to the embedded server: anonymous blank username, blank password and missing password each answer 401 with 'WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...' and an empty body (nothing stored); the same blank username sent with a valid token answers 400. With the loop-7 AuthController (505af8ef) on the same solved work, the anonymous blank and missing fields answered 400. Cause, confirmed by two scratch fixes that each restore 400: a failed @Valid raises MethodArgumentNotValidException, which Spring MVC answers with sendError(400); the container then makes an ERROR dispatch to Boot's /error page, and the Task 2 chain, which ends in anyRequest().authenticated(), authorizes that dispatch too and refuses the anonymous caller with 401. A scratch chain with ERROR dispatches permitted gives 400 for all four blank or missing cases; a scratch AuthController that takes a BindingResult and returns ResponseEntity.badRequest() itself gives 400 for the blank and missing fields with learner work unchanged. MockMvc performs no error dispatch, which is why the lab's own probe saw 400. A second gap in the same validation: a password longer than 72 bytes passes @NotBlank, then Task 1's delegating bcrypt encoder throws IllegalArgumentException 'password cannot be more than 72 bytes' (critic MockMvc probe: ServletException with that root cause); on the embedded server the anonymous caller sees 401, or 500 once ERROR dispatches are permitted, and nothing is stored. The OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet says to enforce a maximum password length of 72 bytes for bcrypt. Low: no test, README step or step 6 row sends a registration (the step 6 check registers through UserAccountService), but the file is shipped as complete code that learners read on a security day, and its comment teaches a status the live app does not give.

findings.recommendation: Keep @Valid and @NotBlank, and add a BindingResult parameter to register that returns ResponseEntity.badRequest().build() when it has errors (critic-tested: anonymous blank and missing fields then answer 400 on the embedded server and all 10 lab tests pass; learner work is unchanged). Add @Size(max = 72) to the password, or a byte-length check, so the bcrypt limit is answered with 400 too. Alternatively permit ERROR dispatches in the Task 2 TODO, as the Spring Security reference suggests, which fixes this and other anonymous error statuses but changes the learner's Task 2. Either way, make the comment match what the running app does, and re-run the registration probe in lab-run.json against the embedded server rather than MockMvc only.

findings.claim: The validation row tells a learner who writes a login that 'without a token the security filter refused this request before it reached the controller, so validation never ran; the request must carry a caller's token'. That is false for a login: /auth/** is permitted, the request reaches AuthController.token, and its own password check answers 401; and login() cannot carry a token, so the advice cannot be followed. The row treats any no-token 401 as a filter refusal (line 379). Critic run at f437bce1a385be8ff0ec5a70d88a607cfd6cf3a1 through the shipped row() wrapper on the solved app: login with a blank username and password, with a blank password, and with a wrong password each get that message in the validation row. A learner who understood the reading can plausibly try this: the topic page pairs validation with bad input, and the loop-8 AuthController now shows Bean Validation on the auth endpoints, beside the step 6 helpers (line 28: a blank field is answered by Bean Validation). The other rows answer logins truthfully (role checks: 'decide what a logged-in caller may do, not whether a login succeeds'; DTO: 'does not give the caller a booking'). Low: the learner still has to find the booking-id constraint, and the message does not let a wrong row pass.

findings.claim: A safe, README-conformant ApiErrors handler fails the required step 6 test with a message that blames the error body. The leak probe judges a returned body by String.valueOf(answer) (line 501), and Spring's ErrorResponse built from the exception prints the wrapped exception, with the probe's marker message, in its toString. Critic run at f437bce1a385be8ff0ec5a70d88a607cfd6cf3a1, JDK 25.0.5, Maven 3.9.16 offline: the private solution with only ApiErrors changed to a NoSuchElementException handler that returns an ErrorResponse with status 404, the title 'Booking not found' and a fixed detail of its own wording fails task7ShowsTheAttackEachPracticeStops with 'answeredBySafeErrorBodies: the error body still reveals the exception'. Every other test passes, and the real 404 bodies for Grace's requests for booking 2 and 999 carry only detail, instance, status and title, with the fixed detail and nothing internal (critic body probe). A scratch test calling the handler directly shows SimpleErrorResponse.toString ending in 'exception=java.util.NoSuchElementException: <the marker>'. ErrorResponse is a documented @ExceptionHandler return type for RFC 9457 problems, listed with ProblemDetail, and README step 4 asks only for 'a 404 problem with the title Booking not found and a fixed detail of your own wording'. A learner who did it right is told it leaks and has no way to find out why. The course pages teach ProblemDetail, not ErrorResponse, so few learners will meet this; it is medium because it rejects a correct completion of a required test with a false message, as cg-sme-apisec-016 did.

Critic acceptance sweep at f437bce1a385be8ff0ec5a70d88a607cfd6cf3a1 (scratch-only subclass of SecurityLabTest calling the five shipped row checks reflectively on the solved app after earlierTasks() returned null): 202 candidates (four callers times 40 method/path forms, including case, trailing and doubled slashes, query, matrix, dot-segment, percent-encoded, leading-zero, overflow, template, space and bad-escape variants, both prerequisite probe paths, /error, /auth/register and /auth/token, plus 42 login forms). No candidate passes two rows, neither probe path passes any row for any caller, and every accepted candidate is an instance of its own practice: a customer reaching the admin statistics endpoint (role checks); a login presenting the copied stored value for one of the three existing accounts (hashing); a non-positive booking id sent with any caller's token (validation); a customer reading a booking of their own (DTO); a token-bearing request for a booking the caller does not own or that does not exist (safe error bodies).
